title: Dragon fruit Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Dragon fruit Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Dragon fruit nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and potassium in saniata, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Dragon fruit nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your saniata (dragon fruit) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, magnesium and iron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But iron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which dragon fruit nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a dragon fruit nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest dragon fruit nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in dragon fruit

No dragon fruit particular description of this shortage was found in an extension source. So this follows general plant signs, read on the green stems that do the work of leaves. The older stem segments turn pale green to yellowish evenly, without spots. New shoots come slowly, stay thin and short, and the plant fills its post slowly. Fewer flowers and smaller fruit follow. You see it most at this stage: young plants growing up the post in the first two years, and bearing plants that are not fed after harvest.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in saniata
Sandy soils low in organic matter, heavy rain that washes nitrogen down, and plants left without fertilizer or manure. Dragon fruit is a heavy feeder even though it is a cactus.
How to tell it apart

Sunburn bleaches the sun facing side of stems yellow to white in patches, while nitrogen shortage pales the whole plant. Stem canker shows small orange to brown spots that sink and crack. To be sure, do a soil test before planting, as Wikifarmer advises. A tissue test of a mature stem section helps.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

UF IFAS gives young plants about 118 grams of a complete fertilizer every two months in the first year, 136 to 182 grams every two months in the second and third years. 227 to 341 grams three to four times a year after that, with manure or compost around the base. In the Philippines, Wikifarmer reports growers giving about 2 kg of organic fertilizer plus 25 grams of Urea 46 0 0 and 75 grams of Complete 14 14 14 per plant every three to six months.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, feed in small, regular doses with plenty of compost or manure, kept a little away from the stem base, as UF IFAS advises.
Potassium deficiency in dragon fruit

No dragon fruit particular description of this shortage was found in an extension source. So this follows general plant signs, read on the green stems that do the work of leaves. Older stem segments yellow and may dry at the edges and tips. Stems get weaker, and fruit come small, light and less sweet. You see it most at this stage: flowering and fruit filling, when the fruit pull the most potash.
Why potassium deficiency happens in saniata
Dragon fruit takes out much more potash than nitrogen. In a UC South Coast trial, harvested fruit and pruned stems removed about two to three times as much potash as nitrogen.
How to tell it apart

Sunburn scorches the sun facing side of the stems. Stem canker and anthracnose leave sunken brown spots spread over the stem, not a drying that starts at the edges of old segments. To be sure, A soil test and a tissue test of a mature stem section. Bigger, heavier fruit after potash is added point to it.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Give more potash than nitrogen once plants bear, using Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Sulfate of potash 0 0 50 with a complete fertilizer. In a Claveria, Misamis Oriental trial on red fleshed dragon fruit, 60 60 120 kg of NPK (N, phosphate, potash) per hectare gave a higher return on investment than 120 120 120, as less nitrogen and phosphorus and more potash paid best. Follow a soil test for the exact rate.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, return pruned stems as compost only if they are healthy, and add potash at every feeding of bearing plants.
Phosphorus deficiency in dragon fruit

No dragon fruit particular description of this shortage was found in an extension source. So this follows general plant signs, read on the green stems that do the work of leaves. Shoots and roots grow slowly, so the plant climbs its post late and makes few new shoots. Stems may look dull dark green. Flowering is poor and fruit numbers drop. You see it most at this stage: young plants after planting, and bearing plants that flower poorly.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in saniata
Acid, weathered soils that hold phosphorus tightly and soils with no phosphate at planting. The Claveria researchers note that phosphorus shortage cuts the growth of shoots and roots.
How to tell it apart

Waterlogged or rotting roots also stunt the plant, so check the roots and drainage. Nitrogen shortage stunts too, but the stems turn pale, not dark. To be sure, A soil test for phosphorus and pH. A tissue test of a mature stem section helps.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Put Superphosphate 0 20 0 or Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0 in the planting hole and at feedings, following a soil test. In a 2019 Claveria, Misamis Oriental trial, 60 300 60 kg of NPK per hectare gave the most flowers, the most fruit per post, the highest yield and the best return, compared with lower phosphorus rates.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add phosphate and compost at planting, and keep soil pH in the range the UC South Coast trial gives, about 5.3 to 6.7, with lime on very acid soils.
Magnesium deficiency in dragon fruit

No dragon fruit particular description of this shortage was found in an extension source. So this follows general plant signs, read on the green stems that do the work of leaves. Since dragon fruit has no true leaves, look at the older stem segments: they lose color and turn yellowish while the young shoots stay green. Fruit quality can drop. You see it most at this stage: bearing plants, especially after heavy potash feeding.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in saniata
Acid, sandy soils that have lost magnesium to rain, and heavy potash use, which competes with magnesium. UF IFAS recommends a fertilizer that carries 2 to 3 percent magnesium.
How to tell it apart

Nitrogen shortage pales the whole plant, young shoots included. Sunburn bleaches only the sun facing side. To be sure, A soil test for magnesium, potash and pH, and a tissue test of an older stem section.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

UF IFAS uses a complete fertilizer with 2 to 3 percent magnesium at every feeding. Magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt) can be added to the soil or sprayed. Follow the label. On acid soils, use Dolomite, which supplies magnesium and raises pH.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use a fertilizer or mix that contains magnesium, and keep potash and magnesium in balance with a soil test.
Iron deficiency in dragon fruit

No dragon fruit particular description of this shortage was found in an extension source. So this follows general plant signs, read on the green stems that do the work of leaves. New shoots and young segments come out pale yellow, while older stems stay green. Growth of new shoots slows. UF IFAS notes that pitaya shows minor element shortages on poor, high pH soils. You see it most at this stage: new growth flushes, in the warm rainy season.
Why iron deficiency happens in saniata
High pH, limestone or coral soils, and soils limed too heavily. Waterlogged soil also cuts iron uptake.
How to tell it apart

Nitrogen shortage pales older stems first. Young shoots are often lighter green for a short time and darken as they mature. To be sure, A soil test with pH. A small test drench of iron on a few plants, watching whether the next shoots come out green.
What to apply for iron deficiency

On high pH soil, UF IFAS drenches each plant with 7 to 15 grams of chelated iron in the first year, rising to 22 to 29 grams per plant in later years. On neutral or acid soil, apply small amounts of Ferrous sulfate at the base. UF IFAS also gives four to six minor element sprays through the warm, rainy season.

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, do not over lime, add plenty of organic matter, and keep the soil well drained.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any dragon fruit nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your saniata needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Dragon fruit nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my saniata leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: stems turn pale green to yellowish all over, new shoots come slowly and thin, and few flowers form. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at iron deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in dragon fruit?
items.a: UF IFAS gives young plants about 118 grams of a complete fertilizer every two months in the first year, 136 to 182 grams every two months in the second and third years. 227 to 341 grams three to four times a year after that, with manure or compost around the base.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in dragon fruit?
items.a: Give more potash than nitrogen once plants bear, using Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Sulfate of potash 0 0 50 with a complete fertilizer. In a Claveria, Misamis Oriental trial on red fleshed dragon fruit, 60 60 120 kg of NPK (N, phosphate, potash) per hectare gave a higher return on investment than 120 120 120, as less nitrogen and phosphorus and more potash paid best.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in dragon fruit?
items.a: Put Superphosphate 0 20 0 or Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0 in the planting hole and at feedings, following a soil test. In a 2019 Claveria, Misamis Oriental trial, 60 300 60 kg of NPK per hectare gave the most flowers, the most fruit per post, the highest yield and the best return, compared with lower phosphorus rates.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my saniata lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the dragon fruit nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
